mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates more weekday movement that spills into shopping and dining trips, so RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep improving but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL falls by more than about 1 point week over week, people spend less time at home and shift into outside errands and discretionary shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 12.4 to 10.6 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below its prior-week level by more than 1 point and RETAIL_REC still falls over the next 14 days, the hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES above their current levels signals looser activity constraints and more commuting intensity, which should lift retail and recreation mobility over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:Both series are less negative at t-0w than at t-3w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both post two-week gains but RETAIL_REC remains below its previous four-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility after a deep trough reflects better outdoor conditions and weekend circulation, which then spills into discretionary retail visits one to four weeks later.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remains highly negative but improved from -65.0 to -59.1 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to recover over the next month but RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the last four weeks, reject this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps improving while WORKPLACES stays depressed, routine errands substitute for broader shopping trips and retail mobility stays flat or declines over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while WORKPLACES remains below -25
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -17.7 to -9.9 while WORKPLACES remained negative
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM strengthens and WORKPLACES stays below -25 yet RETAIL_REC rises above its prior four-week mean, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week acceleration in TRANSIT mobility is an early signal of higher out-of-home activity that should translate into more retail and recreation visits within the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -32.7 at t-1w to -29.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not rise within the next 7 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The retail rebound only appears when BOTH TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL normalize together: more trips away from home plus less time spent indoors should jointly lift RETAIL_REC over a four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL falls below 11
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT became less negative while RESIDENTIAL eased from 12.4 to 10.6
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL falls below 11 but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its previous four-week mean within 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A stable improvement in GROCERY_PHARM is a proxy for broader foot-traffic normalization; if it holds for two more weeks, retail mobility should increase modestly over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved in every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above -12 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not improve over the subsequent 14 to 28 days, the hypothesis is false.
